{{Citation}}
[[File:MainGalaxy.png|thumb|right|250px|A map of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] showing the major routes]]
{{Quote|Make for the closest hyperspace lane you can find, Zee-Thirty-Seven.|[[Griebs Kishpaugh]], to [[Z-37]]|<ref name="The Clone Wars: The Enemy Within">''[[The Clone Wars: The Enemy Within]]''</ref>}}
A '''hyperspace route''', also known as a '''hyperroute''', '''hyperway''', '''hyperlane''', '''hyperspace lane''', '''spacelane''', '''star-route''', '''trade route''', or '''jump route''', was an area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] that had been deemed safe for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel. The largest were known as [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroutes]].

==Overview==
Hyperspace routes were routes through space in which a [[Starship/Legends|spaceship]] could safely travel uninterrupted without colliding with a body in space, or some other phenomenon such as a [[Black hole/Legends|black hole]].<ref name="The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref> There were five major routes in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], with hundreds of secondary routes and thousands of minor ones. Scouting new hyperspace routes was an incredibly dangerous task for an explorer.

Routes had to be surveyed and blazed by [[Scout/Legends|scouts]]. Those daring individuals scanned an unknown area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], made small jumps to safe destinations, repeatedly scanning for obstacles and jumping; when reaching a desired destination, they connected the small trips into an [[astrography|astrographically]] continuous route.<ref name="atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> One such entity responsible for this was the [[Hyperspace Navigator's Guild]].<ref>[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 1]]</ref>

Smaller routes and shortcuts might connect [[star system/Legends|star systems]] that were astrographically close, but this was not always the case; sometimes two locations might belong to different busy and known hyperlanes, in which case a pilot had to divert to a route switch that was traversed by both known lanes. For example, to travel from a location set along the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], to a location found on the [[Corellian Run/Legends|corellian Run]], sometimes a ship had to divert to [[Denon system/Legends|Denon]].<ref name="atlas" />

There were rumors about spacer guilds, shipping companies, scouts, smugglers, species and any kind of spacers that discovered trade routes and shortcuts that they kept secret.<ref name="atlas" />

The natural movement of the galactic bodies as they rotated around the [[Galactic Center]], meant that mapped routes became obsolete within decades. This was common for less-used routes, since busier routes were constantly updated. The [[Space Ministry]] was responsible for this task; its astrogation bureau collected and analyzed data from individual [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputers]] that [[spacer/Legends|spacers]] were obliged to share. Navicomputers were usually freely updated during standard docking precedures.<ref name="atlas" />

In many parts of the galaxy, hyperlanes required periodic re-entry into realspace to manually maneuver the ship towards the next hyper-point. [[Pirate/Legends|Pirate]] raids were common in these spots. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and other governments often sought to lessen this threat by constructing [[Space station/Legends|deep-space platforms]] at hyper-points. [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]] were also deployed.<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>

{{Tech-stub}}

==Major routes==
*'''[[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]]''', established in [[5500 BBY/Legends|5500 BBY]], was a major trade route that ran from [[Abregado-rae/Legends|Abregado-rae]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] to [[Kathol sector/Legends|Kathol sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].
*'''[[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]''' was a vital trade hyperroute that, along with the Corellian Run, made up the border of [[The Slice/Legends|The Slice]].
*'''[[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]]''' was the only hyperlane that crossed the entire galaxy.
*The '''[[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]]''' started at [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], looped around the Deep Core, went through [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], and continued on to pass through [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] before terminating near the remote Outer Rim world of [[Naos III/Legends|Naos III]].
*The '''[[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]]''' began at Corellia and headed in the direction of [[Duro/Legends|Duro]]. It eventually passed by the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] before tapering off.
